question.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{y} \\ {e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$

current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/8b02f8b4b8bfe1dfc91ef70d6014ce541ac9348d4593b8390c3ffde9d6e36e1d.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/072721d659e64ca00d9c25add5e651ebac11b4bf59eeea62a8a3b7320fab1b33.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/8ce9febcf133024ebfff82beabdebea41260b07e482173e6a3fbe061e9cca975.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})=2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{y}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/a4c9e22098aedd60b21d10c9f377ceb0d914291651262bd40eea0ab8aad8c97e.svg)
Thus, the missing entries are $y,\:$ $0,\:$ and $\ln{x}.$
